about.title: Albany Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast — a wet floor near Solano Avenue, a cracked walkway off Marin, poor lighting in a Marin corridor parking structure. What matters afterward is what you can show. California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. That's the heart of most Albany premises liability disputes, and it's why documenting the scene and preserving surveillance footage early matters so much. Business and building surveillance systems in Albany often overwrite footage within days or weeks, so timing can affect what evidence survives. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects people injured on someone else's property with an independent attorney who can evaluate the notice question, gather evidence, and explain your options. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers on your behalf, and reaching out costs you nothing.

whyChoose.title: Why Albany Fall Victims Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises law hinges on whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An independent attorney can help identify evidence — like prior complaints or inspection logs — that speaks directly to that notice question.

items.title: We Know Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance video from a Solano Avenue storefront or a San Pablo corridor building can be overwritten within days. Connecting with an attorney quickly can help preserve footage and hazard photos before they're gone.

items.title: We Understand Comparative Fault
items.desc: California applies pure comparative fault, meaning a partial share of blame doesn't automatically bar recovery — it can reduce it proportionally. An independent attorney can help present your case in a way that accounts for this rule.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Albany?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If a public entity owns or maintains the property — say a sidewalk or public building — that deadline is much shorter, sometimes just months. Because Albany includes both private storefronts and municipal property, it's worth having an attorney confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for my own fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partially at fault doesn't automatically end your claim. Instead, any compensation can be reduced by your percentage of responsibility. An independent attorney can help evaluate how the facts of your fall might be viewed under this rule.

items.question: Does Albany's crash and injury data relate to slip and fall cases?
items.answer: Not directly — public crash counts for Albany reflect traffic collisions, not premises falls. But the underlying idea is similar: incidents cluster around high-traffic times and locations, and the same is often true for falls at busy retail or residential properties along corridors like Solano or San Pablo. Documenting exactly where and when your fall happened still matters.

items.question: Who pays if I'm connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: LawProactive doesn't charge anything to connect you with an independent attorney. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover compensation for you. There's no upfront cost to have your situation reviewed.
